# CYBOU

CYBOU is a sovereign cybersecurity, communications and data infrastructure designed
in France around an open-source Full Node P2P core. It provides protocol-level
foundations for cryptographic identity, end-to-end encrypted messaging (Mail), and
distributed encrypted storage (Files), without dependence on a foreign SaaS control plane.

## Product verticals and architecture

```text
                           CYBOU
                             │
                     Shared CYBOU Core
                 (Open-source trust core)
                             │
            ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐
            ▼                                 ▼
      CYBOU Public                      CYBOU Enterprise
   (One shared network)             (Private CYBOU networks)
            │                                 │
   Reference deployment              Organization trust domain
   France-first public IP policy     Custom admission (VPN, LAN, CIDR)
   CYBOU-operated PoA                Organization-controlled PoA
   Community ecosystem               Enterprise tooling (planned)
```

- **Shared CYBOU Core:** Native C++20 Full Node, P2P protocol, cryptographic Identity
  with separated roles (Ed25519, ML-DSA-44/65, X-Wing), generic `RootPublication`,
  BLAKE3-256 chunk trees, deterministic state execution, and clean-machine recovery.
- **CYBOU Public:** The single public reference network demonstrating the technology,
  using an offline-signed public genesis, CYBOU-operated PoA finalizer, and a public-IP
  admission policy restricted to French IP space.
- **CYBOU Enterprise:** Commercial B2B product direction enabling organizations to deploy
  independent private CYBOU networks with their own NetworkID, signed genesis, PoA
  authority, and network perimeter (corporate VPN, internal LAN, CIDR allowlists),
  coupled with enterprise management tooling, deployment services, and SLA support.

*Policy note:* French public-IP admission is a deployment policy of the public CYBOU
network, not an intrinsic limitation of the CYBOU protocol.

## Current implementation status

- **Development state:** Active development on the DEVNET test network. MAINNET is
  unprovisioned. Enterprise private provisioning and management tooling are in active
  product development and do not yet constitute an off-the-shelf commercial product.
- **Consensus & finality:** Canonical finality is hybrid post-quantum Proof-of-Authority (PoA)
  authorized by network genesis (operated by CYBOU on DEVNET; controlled directly by the organization
  on private enterprise networks). Every full node independently validates blocks, state roots,
  and PoA certificates against genesis authority.
- **Application plane:** Mail and Files expose familiar desktop workflows over generic
  `RootPublication` and BLAKE3 chunk trees. All application payloads and indexes are
  encrypted client-side. The protocol contains no universal decryption key.
- **Storage durability:** DEVNET requires one remote replica; Beta targets two independent
  remote replicas (local cache excluded). Distinguishing proven StorageIds does not establish
  independent physical disks, hosts, or operators. GET/hash verification establishes
  availability at check time, not continuous retention proof.
- **Post-quantum profile:** DEVNET pins the experimental X-Wing / HPKE IETF draft-05 profile
  and OpenSSL 3.5+ ML-KEM/ML-DSA primitives. This is not an external security certification.
- **Regulatory readiness:** The project evaluates RGPD, NIS 2, CRA, and French cryptology
  frameworks as engineering targets. The software is not certified by ANSSI, HDS, or GDPR auditors.

## Commercial & GTM model

- **First adoption unit:** Organization/team (no isolated consumer launch).
- **Target customers:** French and European enterprises, PME/ETI, critical infrastructure
  operators, and teams handling sensitive communications or intellectual property.
- **Immediate objective:** Design partners and structured B2B pilots (20–100 users, 8–12 weeks).
- **Economics:** Internal deterministic resource budgeting (System Balance, fees, storage rent).
  No ICO, no public token sale, no cryptocurrency exchange listing objective.
